content: 1. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the effectiveness of the quadrivalent intranasal influenza virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Additionally, immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 2. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate diminishes the effects of the trivalent influenza virus vaccine (both intranasal and recombinant forms) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also heighten the risk of infection when administered with live vaccines. 3. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and inotuzumab ozogamicin both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 4. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate enhances the effects of insulin aspart, insulin aspart protamine, insulin degludec, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin isophane human, and insulin regular human. This interaction may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Dosage adjustments of insulin and other antidiabetic drugs may be necessary. Close monitoring is advised. 5. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and isavuconazonium sulfate both reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 10. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 11.
